claim_being_audited: That the model can be certified for launch now because aggregate readiness passed, rehearsal had no severity-one incidents, and a 7% reversible rollout with monitoring is sufficient so long as the packet frames the exposed public-benefits limitation as a disclosed model-card limitation rather than a fully mitigated issue.
decision_criteria: Use compliant only if admissible evidence shows the material limitation is either resolved, explicitly disclosed in the launch documentation, or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
Treat rollout controls and monitoring as mitigating context, not as a substitute for the required disclosure predicate when the affected segment remains exposed.
Downgrade support when the packet accurately identifies the policy issue but the record lacks the artifact needed to prove the action is actually compliant.
evidence_requests: Provide the final model card or launch artifact showing explicit disclosure of the public benefits eligibility limitation.
Provide approved risk acceptance if the organization intends to rely on that path instead of disclosure.
Provide the final certification record showing whether certification is conditioned on that disclosure before launch.
specific_concerns: The affected public benefits eligibility segment remains exposed in the initial rollout cohort.
Policy text requires disclosure unless the limitation is resolved or covered by approved risk acceptance before launch.
The available risk acceptance is only a draft, has a blank approver line, and does not mention the exposed public benefits eligibility segment.
The evidence shows that disclosure is required, but does not show that the required disclosure has actually been completed in the launch artifact.
Rollout controls, small percentage rollout, rollback, and monitoring do not by themselves satisfy the policy when the affected use case remains exposed.
unsupported_claims: The recommended action to certify now is not fully supported because there is no admissible evidence of a completed model-card disclosure or an approved risk acceptance covering the exposed segment.
Any implication that rollout controls alone make the launch compliant would be unsupported by the governing policy text.
